targets.label: abrupt, spectral peak
targets.note: READ AS A PEAK VALUE HERE. Demo 17c reads the same published 2340 pm/V as a value AT 1550 nm and anchors on it there; demo17c.yaml records that reading. The two readings cannot both hold, because our spectrum's peak/1550 contrast is 1.72 and the 2340/1150 pair implies 2.03. Which is right changes which combination wins, so `--targets-profile demo17c` switches to the other reading and prints the whole table again.

targets.label: abrupt, at 1550 nm
targets.source: arXiv:2602.23246v1 Section 3.1, abrupt value at the 1550 nm design point
targets.note: Paired with abrupt_peak above. Together they fix the paper's implied peak/1550 contrast at 2.03 against our 1.72 -- a 15 % SHAPE difference that no scalar multiplier can remove, which is the main finding here.

targets.label: graded, spectral peak
targets.note: The paper quotes 1200 pm/V (EDS Al profile) and 1363 pm/V (EDS Ga profile) for graded interfaces. Only the 1200 is scored, as requested; demo17c.yaml carries the pair as a band.

factors.label: tensor-component inversion
factors.rationale: NO SOURCE IN THIS REPOSITORY ESTABLISHES THIS FACTOR. It is carried because it was asked for and because its size is worth seeing, not because anything supports it. Two things to note. First, no audit here has measured a tensor-inversion ratio at all -- Demos 16F, 17b and 18 swept N_z, permutation, spin and the unit-cell dipole, and none of them produced a 2.8. Second, 3.0 * 3.0 * 2.8 * 1.1 = 27.72, which is the measured residual 27.63 to within 0.3 %, so this value looks reverse-engineered from the gap rather than derived from a tensor relation. A factor chosen to close a gap cannot then be evidence that the gap is closed.

combinations.description: Every candidate at its largest, product 27.72 against a measured residual of 27.63. CONSTRUCTED TO CLOSE THE GAP: reproducing 2340 pm/V at 1550 nm is therefore arithmetic, exactly as Demo 17c's fitted K is arithmetic, and is not evidence. What it does show honestly is where the OTHER published numbers land once the 1550 nm one is forced.

factors.label: DFT unit-cell dipole tweak
factors.rationale: POINTS THE WRONG WAY. Demo 17b sweep D evaluated the Kane relation r = (hbar/E_g) sqrt(E_p / 2 m_0) for GaAs and got 0.736 nm against the published 0.751 nm -- a multiplier of 0.96, slightly BELOW one, and a 2 % confirmation that the published constant is right. Raising the dipole by 10 % (chi(2) by 1.1x) is not supported by that measurement; it is carried so its contribution to Combo 10 stays visible.

ranking.caveat: Every multiplier here is DECLARED, not derived. A combination that lands near a published number has not thereby been shown to be the right physics: the sweep resolves the product of four factors and can never attribute it, two of the ten combinations are numerically identical by different routes, and one was constructed from the known residual. Read the ranking as a map of what each hypothesis would imply, not as evidence for any of them.

shape_versus_scale.definition: spectral peak divided by the value at 1550 nm, same case
shape_versus_scale.why_it_matters: a scalar multiplier cannot change a ratio, so this mismatch survives every combination in the ensemble and sets a floor on how well any of them can do on both quantities at once

permutation.note: 2.0 and 3.0 are two readings of the SAME piece of bookkeeping, so a combination must not carry both. Demo 17b flagged this explicitly: the Bloembergen/Boyd degenerate-SHG factor is what a permutation sum over the two input photons produces, and Demo 16F measured Eq.1/Eq.2 = 3.000000 with no permutation sum applied. No combination below multiplies them.
permutation.why_not: each combination states one value per factor, so two readings of the same counting cannot compound within a row
